dropped.item: Module versioning: versioning of the project is idiomatic of a Go project using Go modules (link to https://golang.org/ref/mod#versions)
Module versioning: Semantic import versioning will be used (link to golang/go wiki Modules#semantic-import-versioning)
Module versioning: versions will comply with semver 2.0 (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html)

If a module is version v2 or higher, the major version must be included as `/vN` at the end of module paths in go.mod files (e.g., `module go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2`, `require go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2 v2.0.1`) and in the package import path (e.g., `import "go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2/component"`)
The `/vN` suffix also applies to paths used in `go get` commands (e.g., `go get go.opentelemetry.io/collector/v2@v2.0.1`), which contains both a `/v2` and a `@v2.0.1`
If a module is version v0 or v1, do not include the major version in either the module path or the import path

Semantic convention packages contain a complete version identifier in their import path to enable concurrent use of multiple convention versions in a single application; this identifies the specification version used to generate the package and is unrelated to the module version
A single module should exist, rooted at the top level of the repository, containing all packages provided for use outside the repository

Additional modules may be created in the repository to isolate build-time tools, other commands, or independent libraries, and such modules should be versioned in sync with the `go.opentelemetry.io/collector` module

Experimental modules still under active development are versioned with major version v0 to imply the semver stability guarantee (semver spec-item-4), quoted as: "Major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development. Anything MAY change at any time. The public API SHOULD NOT be considered stable."

Versioning of the associated contrib repository (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib) is idiomatic of a Go project using Go modules, uses semantic import versioning, and complies with semver 2.0

Contrib v2+ module path example: `module github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/processor/k8sprocessor/v2`, `require ... v2.0.1`, import path `"github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/processor/k8sprocessor/v2"`, and `go get .../k8sprocessor/v2@v2.0.1`
Contrib: if a module is version v0 or v1, do not include the major version in the module path or import path
Contrib modules encapsulate receivers, processors, exporters, extensions, connectors and any other independent sets of related components
Contrib experimental modules are versioned with major version v0 (with the semver 0.y.z quote)
Contrib experimental modules start versioning at v0.0.0, increment the minor version for backwards incompatible changes and the patch version for backwards compatible changes
Mature contrib modules with a guaranteed stable public API are versioned with major version v1 or greater
All stable contrib modules of the same major version as this project use the same entire version

Stable modules may be released with an incremented minor or patch version even when the module's code has not changed, the only change being an update of the module's dependency on this project's stable APIs
Contrib modules will be kept up to date with this project's releases
GitHub releases will be made for all releases
Go modules will be made available at Go package mirrors

dropped.item: The "Examples" section introduction stating the examples show two capabilities users frequently rely on: batching by client metadata and buffering the queue on disk
The `metadata_keys` setting forms a distinct batch for each combination of `client.Metadata` values, enabling a multi-tenant pipeline to batch each tenant's data separately
The queue/batch processor offers this partitioning behavior through the `batch::partition::metadata_keys` setting

Example YAML for partitioning: otlp receiver with grpc protocol and `include_metadata: true`, `processors: queuebatch: batch: partition: metadata_keys: [tenant_id]`, and a traces pipeline with receivers [otlp], processors [queuebatch], exporters [otlp]
Receivers must be configured with `include_metadata: true` so the metadata keys are available to the processor
An empty metadata value and unset metadata are treated as distinct cases
Metadata key entries are case-insensitive
By default the queue is held in memory, so any buffered data is lost if the Collector stops
Set the top-level `storage` field to the ID of a storage extension to persist the queue on disk, so buffered data is recovered and exporting continues after a restart

Example YAML for persistence: `extensions: file_storage: directory: /var/lib/otelcol/queuebatch`, `processors: queuebatch: storage: file_storage`, `service: extensions: [file_storage]` and a logs pipeline with receivers [otlp], processors [queuebatch], exporters [otlp]
When `storage` is set there is no in-memory queue; each request is serialized as it enters the queue and read back from disk before export
The `wait_for_result` setting is not supported together with `storage`
Link to the filestorage extension: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/storage/filestorage
